result.summary: Document in the libbitcoinkernel API header that btck_chainstate_manager_process_block treats passed blocks as requested. It warns consumers that callers accepting blocks from untrusted sources must apply pre-filtering checks themselves to avoid storing unwanted or low-work blocks.
result.problem: The C API header for btck_chainstate_manager_process_block does not document that it sets force_processing, meaning the validation engine treats every block as requested and bypasses checks like min chain work or tip work comparisons before storing to disk.
evidence: Commit ed2c4a344a: 'btck_chainstate_manager_process_block processes every block as requested... The API does not say so. Document that a caller taking blocks from untrusted sources has to apply these checks itself.'
result.scope_notes: A documentation-only change to the libbitcoinkernel public interface header.
result.card: Documents in the libbitcoinkernel header that btck_chainstate_manager_process_block treats all blocks as requested, storing them without standard pre-filtering against the tip or minimum chain work. This informs kernel API consumers accepting blocks from untrusted sources that they must perform filtering checks themselves. The change consists of a four-line documentation addition to the kernel C API.

risk.why: This is a documentation-only addition to a header file with no runtime code modifications.
